references.text: The prophet Isaiah speaks of being struck and not hiding one's face from shame, which can be seen as a parallel to not denying the faith even under persecution.
David expresses trust in God that is not ashamed of him, reflecting the theme of mutual recognition between God and humanity.
Jesus warns about the shame of denying him before people, which is a direct parallel to Matthew 10:33.
Paul speaks of not denying Christ through actions, which can be seen as an extension of the idea of not denying him in words.
The book of Revelation promises recognition before the Father for those who overcome, mirroring the promise of mutual recognition in Matthew 10:33.
